subject.title: fix(openclaw): prevent private state races during publication

question: Should identity-checked mutation claims and strict ownership or ACL validation become the permanent fail-closed boundary for existing Crabline private-file publication and cleanup?
rationale: The PR deliberately changes which existing filesystem states are trusted and can turn ownership or ACL drift into publication or cleanup failure; tests alone cannot decide whether that compatibility tradeoff matches maintainer security policy.

options.title: Approve after platform proof
options.body: Accept the boundary after clean Linux and native Windows runtime evidence covers attacks, races, stale claims, cleanup identity changes, and existing-path upgrades.

options.title: Preserve compatibility mode
options.body: Keep compatible handling as the default and introduce strict fail-closed validation only through an explicitly approved migration or policy control.

options.title: Split the hardening
options.body: Pause this combined rewrite and land smaller ancestry, claim, and cleanup changes with independent security review and proof.

recommendation.title: Approve after platform proof
recommendation.body: Accept the boundary after clean Linux and native Windows runtime evidence covers attacks, races, stale claims, cleanup identity changes, and existing-path upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the repository-member author of the complete proposed security-boundary design and its focused test expansion.
